title: My Interview at Jooyeshgar: A Good Small Company
excerpt: My interview at Jooyeshgar was a pleasant surprise. A small active company with logical people, a quick test, and no strange challenges.

blocks.text: Jooyeshgar Company
Jooyeshgar is a small company with few people but apparently active!
Overall, Jooyeshgar was a reasonable and good company. I can describe it like this: my impression was that it can be a suitable starting point for a professional career.
Today I had an interview at 10 AM, I arrived on time and when I entered and introduced myself I was faced with an environment that was small. A small office unit with about 10 employees.
The Form and the Test
They gave me an information form and again it was one of those forms whose information is in the resume, but with the difference that this time they had really seen my resume.
They also gave another form that had 10 questions and I had 10 minutes to solve these questions. The questions were more of the challenging and complicated type, like this question:
Ali is at a higher altitude than Ahmad, Kazem is also at a higher altitude than Ali. Who has the highest altitude?
Or for example, certain people went on a trip by plane, certain others went on foot, certain people are happy, which people who went on foot are not happy?

It was this type of question, and I got 9 out of 10 and the reason was that I didn't have the patience to sit and think a lot on the last question, it was really boring and I submitted it earlier than the 10-minute deadline, I submitted it within 8 minutes.
The Interview
After this, I entered the interview, with the company boss and a person from their technical team.

The first question that person asked was to explain the last project you worked on in the field of AI and I started telling it and expressing the challenges I had faced. That person also asked questions and tried to challenge me, but well, more professional than these talks of mine to be able to challenge me 😅 I just wanted to praise myself a bit.
Then the interview with the company boss started, and he said, well, did you see our site? I said yes, he said, in your opinion how can we add AI to it? I said, don't bring AI into it in any way.
For a moment everyone went into shock.
And I explained to them that really this AI hype that has happened doesn't require everyone to go towards it and want to use AI and bring up a chatbot.

He started saying that for example we have 80 thousand registered users and... I said well, in your opinion how many people can this chatbot answer? He said 10-20 people, and I honestly said, really in my opinion this work isn't justified, to bring up a heavy feature for 10-20 people.

Of course he said that well an LLM CALL is simple and there's an API behind it and so on, which here I doubted a bit, because really taking these things to PRODUCTION is hard work and it's not as easy as looking at it as a simple API Call.
They also asked from these questions of whether I use agents or not? How much do I use? Whether I'm familiar with A2A and MCP and Tool and these or not.
My Questions and the Process
Then I started asking questions about what project they actually need me for - what are the working hours and... and they gave me good explanations.
Anyway, the interview lasted about 40 minutes and they honestly told me they set aside this week for interviews and next week they'll inform the result.

Their work process was also that they give a percentage of the main amount for salary in the first month, so we work as a test, and then we go for the main contract and main salary. In my opinion it's not bad.
They also had no objection to my initial offer which was 40 million tomans.
Final Summary

Jooyeshgar was a good company, it was suitable and they had good behavior. In my opinion they won't have heavy and strange challenges and it will be a suitable company to work at. They were really friendly and were also logical and good people.
Again I repeat that: this experience of mine was obtained only from interviewing with this company and according to themselves, by next week they're supposed to inform what the result will be.
